task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 18, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper news update about Hearthline Appliances ending new sales of its extended service plan and the consequences for existing plan holders.

facts.text: Hearthline Appliances said Tuesday, Aug. 18, 2026, that it will stop selling its Extra Years service plan after Sept. 30.
The retailer's 14 stores will continue selling appliances, parts and separately priced repair visits.
There are approximately 14,000 active Extra Years contracts, according to the retailer's account records.
Those contracts will remain administered by the existing provider, Cinder Service Network, until their stated expiration dates.
The active-contract count is not a count of distinct households because some customers hold plans for several appliances.
The sales decision does not alter the written manufacturer warranties supplied with appliances.

Hearthline says its renewed agreement with Cinder increased the one-time administration charge on each newly sold plan from $22 to $31; this is a retailer cost, not a new charge to existing plan holders.
The company has not disclosed the average retail plan price or its margin, so the fee increase does not establish its total profit change.
Chief commercial officer Nessa Flint said sales staff will no longer receive commissions for new service-plan sales after the cutoff.
Staff will receive a temporary three-month commission supplement, but the amount will vary with their prior sales.
Cinder's stated process for existing claims begins with a telephone assessment before an in-home appointment is scheduled.
Cinder's July 2026 report gives a median of eight calendar days from completed telephone assessment to the first home visit among visits completed in this service region that month.
That median excludes still-pending visits and any later parts orders; it is not a maximum wait or a measure of time to a completed repair.
Customer Dane Voss has a refrigerator plan expiring in 2028 and said he initially thought the sales announcement ended his coverage.
Voss said, "I wanted to know who would answer the phone, not whether they would sell me another leaflet."
Flint said, "Stopping new sales does not move an existing repair request to the back of a different queue."
The retailer plans to mail active contract holders a notice naming their provider and expiration date.
No blanket cancellation refund or automatic plan extension is part of the announced change.
Hearthline began selling service plans in 2014, after previously offering repairs only on a per-visit basis.
The reporting record contains no regulator assessment of the plans' value or finding that every claim has been handled correctly.

forbidden_additions: Existing plans are canceled or all 14,000 contracts belong to different households
An eight-day maximum repair guarantee, blanket refund or regulatory endorsement
